newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO seen steady, cash fundamentals soft.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO seen steady, cash fundamentals soft.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices were assessed steady on Monday despite soft physical undertones as bids were expected to stay firm, traders said.
They said strong bids from two local companies may help to push prices higher but supplies in the market is adequate to meet demand.
Physical 180-centistoke cargoes for October lifting were quoted at $120-$121 per tonne on Friday. On Monday, offers were seen at $120.50 for end October lifting.

A trader told Reuters that at least a million tonnes of fuel oil from the Middle East will arrive in the second half of October. While part of the supplies have already been sold, some cargoes were still uncommitted, the trader said.
A major said the bunker market is also weak, potentially placing pressure on cargo prices.
He assessed a support level for 180-cst cargoes, loading in end October/early November at $120 per tonne.
Premiums on the free-on-board Singapore basis were assessed at $2.00-$2.50.
Chinese bids remained low at $125 per tonne for delivery to south China in October.
October swaps were quoted higher at $119.25-$120, compared to Friday's $118.75/$119.50.
Low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) prices were expected to edge lower as the latest KEPCO tender was awarded at a low of $1.91 per barrel over the Singapore quotes.
Traders said the awarded price was 50 cents below KEPCO's last tender, indicating that the market is weak.
